summary: Eiko Okukaze works in Buddhist studies. Okukaze was a doctoral student at Bukkyo University (attested 2010) and is attested as a commissioned researcher at Koyasan University in 2026.

Eileen Power (1889–1940) was a historian and archaeologist. She studied at Oxford High School, Girton College, and the University of Paris, and later held posts at the London School of Economics (~1921–1940) and the University of London (~1931–1940).

Eisaku Okada works in Buddhist studies and studied at Kyoto University (attested 2014). Okada held positions at Koyasan University, Kyoto University, and the Japan Society for the Promotion of Science.
Eisei Kojima was a scholar of Buddhist studies. In 1976, Kojima is attested as holding posts as a professor at Ryukoku University and as president of Doho University.

Eishu Miyazaki (1913–1997) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Japanology. Miyazaki studied at Rissho University under Gyōō Kageyama and later held posts at Rissho University and Minobusan University.
Eishun Fushimi is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. Fushimi studied at the University of Hamburg (attested 1998) under David P. Jackson.

Eivind Kahrs is a scholar in Indology and linguistics. Kahrs taught Aleix Ruiz-Falqués, held a post at Queens' College, Cambridge (attested 2010), and is attested as a Council Member of the Pali Text Society in 2026.
Eizan Tatsuta (1893–1979) was a scholar in religious and Buddhist studies who studied under Sokatsu Shaku and founded Ningen Zen.

Ekai Kawaguchi (1866–1945) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied at Toyo University, Sera Monastery, and Central Hindu College under teachers including Sarat Chandra Das. He served as a professor at Toyo University in 1916.

Ekyo Uno specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. Uno held posts as a lecturer at Osaka University of Foreign Studies (attested 1991) and as a commissioned researcher at Honganji-ha Shōgakuin (attested 1998).
Elaine Fisher is a scholar in Indology and religious studies who was a doctoral student at Columbia University (attested 2010). She holds a faculty post at Stanford University (attested 2026).

Eleanor Nesbitt (born 1951) is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. She studied at Girton College and the University of Oxford, founded the Punjab Research Group, and became emerita professor in Education Studies at the University of Warwick (~1989).

Eleanor Rosch (born 1938) works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She completed her Ph.D. at Harvard University under Roger Brown (~1963–1969) and became a professor of cognitive psychology at the University of California, Berkeley in 1971.

Elena Bashir specializes in linguistics and Indology. After studying at the University of Michigan (until 1988), she joined the University of Chicago in 2000, where she is also attested on an editorial board in 2026.

Elena De Rossi Filibeck is a Tibetologist who studied East Asian history at Sapienza University of Rome under Luciano Petech until 1971. In 1980, she became an associate professor at Sapienza University of Rome.
Elena France Hanson is a scholar in Buddhist studies and religious studies. Hanson earned a Doctor of Philosophy at Harvard University under the supervision of Charles Hallisey (attested 1998).

Elena Mucciarelli is a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at the University of Tübingen. She held posts at Tübingen and was appointed Assistant Professor for Hinduism in the Sanskrit Tradition at the University of Groningen in 2020.

Eli Franco (born 1953) is a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied under Charles Malamoud and habilitated at Hamburg. He held the chair of Indology at Leipzig University (2004–2021) along with posts at Vienna and La Trobe.

Elijah Sacvan Ary (born 1972) works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Sera Monastery, INALCO, and Harvard University, completing his PhD under Janet Gyatso and Leonard W. J. van der Kuijp, and studied under Geshe Karma Sonam.

Eliot Deutsch (1931–2020) was a philosopher and Indologist who earned his Ph.D. at Columbia University. He served as a philosophy professor at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute (1960–1967) and the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (1967–2006).
